annotations.text: No sign-in by design, so something has to stand in. A picker over the 900 real policyholders is the honest answer, and it doubles as the front door.

Direction C's look on a single form, not one question per screen — five round trips to get a quote is tedious in a demo you walk someone through in fifteen minutes.

Sex is in the CSVs but carries no weight in the risk model, so it is off the form.

The breakdown is exact: 45 + 18 + 12 = 75.

But the generator adds a random N(45,15) base per policyholder, so the app can never reproduce a score already in the data.

The CSVs carry no names, only policy_id, so a policy is identified by number alone rather than inventing a field the dataset does not have.

A new policy also gets an exact premium, where every generated one carries ±5% noise.

Temperature and portion are bands, not readings. Severity drives the assessed amount, so the claimant never types a figure.

Still open: whether to warn here when the annual cap is already spent.
$62.77 assessed → trimmed to the $60 cap → less the $5 deductible → $55.00. Real numbers from CLM-000059, and the refusal beneath it is the claim that actually followed, CLM-000060.

All nine events, not just the five claims. Attach only filed claims to the policyholder object and claim frequency stops being computable.

This policy paid out $193.43 against $93.87 of premium — a loss ratio of 2.06.
Reachable within a minute of starting the app: accept a quote and this is what you see. A policy with zero events is a valid state, not an error.

The screen the developer edits in journey 4. Identical to screen 4 but for the two questions and the banner — which is the point: Grail keeps Python attributes in dynamic instance variables, so there is nothing to migrate.

The one real lesson is that older claims need a class-level default, or reading claim.flavour raises AttributeError.

Not an alternative look — a second audience. The policyholder screens answer "what am I owed"; this answers "which plan is losing money", which is exactly what CUJ-2 asks the AI. Sketched in its own idiom; it would want reworking into C's vocabulary if we build it.
